topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by connecting it to earlier histopathology practicals and outlining the day's learning outcomes on cellular transformation and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Discovery and experimental assessment of transforming oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and led to experimental assays for evaluating transforming capacity in the laboratory.

topics.label: Classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the functional distinctions between oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes and demonstrate how their mutations perturb cellular regulation and phenotype.

topics.label: Cellular mechanisms of sequence and chromosomal instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how specific failures in DNA repair, replication fidelity, and chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the cumulative acquisition or germline inheritance of mutations accelerates multi-step tumor development and influences cancer progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes, inviting questions, and recommending external reading before the next session.
